question: Can the canonical reset payload answer exact queries by predecessor search, and what is its cost relative to scanning and dense phase caching on the same inputs?
unit: One fixed profile/query corpus and one local-process timing block. Repeated query values are dependent and do not count as independent application samples.
corpora: All distinct (case_id,m) target profiles from all1622 admitted existing family entries and P=1..4p. Include both no-pruning and pruning profiles.
All112 existing seed20261022 random sparse profiles at g=2^61-1 and t=1,2,3,8,32,128,512,16 instances each, regenerated byte-identically to the existing R32 input hashes.
All6 existing large analytic profiles at g=2^61-1,t=1024,4096,16384,all-survive and one-dominator; regenerate the same old seeded stream and verify canonical hashes.
correctness: Exhaust all15420 existing small profiles and all phases; compare direct raw terms with canonical scan and predecessor. For the complete source family compare every physical P phase against direct triples. For old wide profiles verify all retained reset neighbors for t<=512, plus256 seeded phases per profile; analytic large cases include selected reset boundaries and256 seeded phases. Preserve all counterexamples/failures.
dense_cap: At most2^20 phases per individual profile (16MiB signed128 values); unavailable above the cap. Report unavailable cells explicitly, never as slower timings. Dense tables preserve every phase and may win in the small family.
implementation: One compiled C++17 program, signed128 exact arithmetic, identical immutable input/query arrays. Pre-reduce phases once for every route; optimized scans use conditional wrap rather than a division per term. Record actual compiler flags/version and local CPU/OS, no affinity/process/service changes.
schedule: Nine paired timing blocks. Shuffle the order of the four eligible routes within each corpus/block with fixed seed20261023. One untimed warm pass. Check sums outside timing and retain a volatile checksum so computations cannot be removed. No background process termination or global priority changes.
queries: Same seeded stream per corpus for every route and block. Family corpus:2^20 queries cycling all target profiles with uniform phase in the profile modulus. Wide corpus:2^15 queries per distinct original t/kind stratum, cycling every profile in that stratum; all112 random and6 analytic cases included. Seed20261023. Store the generated stream or its deterministic algorithm and checksum.
timing_metrics: Construction wall time separately for grouping/canonical conversion/predecessor sorting/dense table. Hot query wall time and median/min/max across9 paired blocks; preserve all per-block values and route order. Ratios are corpus-specific local implementation results, not hardware/cache/application speedups or confidence intervals.
memory_metrics: Profile term counts, reset-pair counts, dense scalar counts, and actual array-capacity bytes using recorded C++sizeof values. Exclude allocator/process/runtime overhead explicitly; no minimum encoded-byte claim.
prospective_g: Check g*=lcm gcd(P_i,d) for fixed portfolios: all P<=4p; singleton P=2p; pair P=2p and3p. Report all forced-full cases and storage/support counts, not only compact wins. This is a mathematical validation, not a workload-frequency estimate.
analysis: No significance test or population inference. The same host supplies9 timing blocks; they measure run-to-run variability only. Report dense-cache wins, lookup losses, modest canonical-only gains and every unavailability. Stop on a correctness failure; repair in a new preserved attempt before interpreting timings.
